He is the cousin of basketball hall of famer [[Grant Hill]]. {{Cite web | title=ANOTHER ALEXANDER HEADING TO VIRGINIA | url=https://scholar.lib.vt.edu/VA-news/ROA-Times/issues/1994/rt0994/940921/09230054.htm | access-date=2026-08-02 | website=scholar.lib.vt.edu}} His son, Courtney Jason Alexander II, played college basketball at Tennessee Tech from 2015–2019.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ttusports.com/sports/mbkb/2015-16/bios/alexander_ii_courtney_mcni|title=Courtney Alexander II|website=Tennessee Tech}} ==Career== After playing high school basketball at [[Masuk High School]] in [[Monroe, Connecticut]], Alexander moved to [[Durham, North Carolina]], to play for [[Charles E. Jordan High School|C. E. Jordan High School]] to finish his high school career. A [[shooting guard]], he played [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Virginia]] and [[California State University, Fresno|Fresno State]], and he led the nation in scoring in the 1999–2000 season at Fresno State. He was selected by the [[Orlando Magic]] with the 13th overall pick in the [[2000 NBA draft]]; his rights were traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on the same day. He played for the Mavericks before being traded during his rookie season to the [[Washington Wizards]], where he played until 2002. He was named to the All-Rookie second team. He was then traded in the offseason to the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. A highlight of his career was a 33-point effort for the Wizards against the [[Toronto Raptors]] on April 18, 2001,{{cite web|title=Toronto Raptors at Washington Wizards, April 18, 2001|department=Basketball-Reference|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200104180WAS.html|access-date=January 20, 2019}} when [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]] was out with injuries. He suffered a tear of his Achilles' tendon in 2003 while with the Hornets, and after rehabilitating his injury, he signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] but was released before ever playing a game for them due to an injury to the tendons in his left foot.https://www.fresnobee.com/sports/story/11813004p-12529547c.html{{Dead link | date=August 2026 | fix-attempted=yes}} On October 8, 2006, Alexander was signed by the [[Denver Nuggets]]{{cite news|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2006/10/08/former-first-rounder-alexander-signs-on/|work=Denver Post|author=Delander, Brady|title=Former first-rounder Alexander signs on|date=October 8, 2006|access-date=January 20, 2019}} after being out of the league for three seasons, but was waived on October 15.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/transactions|title=ESPN - NBA Basketball Transactions|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=January 20, 2019}} Because of his 3-year hiatus and being waived in October 2006 by the Nuggets before ever playing a game for them, Alexander's final NBA game was actually on May 2, 2003, in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference first round against the Philadelphia 76ers. In that game, he only recorded 2 points as the Hornets wrist the series 4–2 and were eliminated from the playoffs. ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===Regular season=== {{NBA
